summary: The health-tech sector is moving rapidly across multiple fronts, with significant funding flowing into mental health platforms and biotech innovation. InStride closed a $30 million Series C for pediatric mental health, while MultiValent Biotherapies raised $27 million to develop a dual-targeting prostate cancer drug, signaling continued investor confidence in specialized healthcare solutions. On the regulatory and operational side, the FDA's new Bayesian guidance is reshaping clinical trial design toward greater flexibility, potentially accelerating development timelines for complex diseases like rare cancers. Technology applications are expanding into public health surveillance, with Verily using wastewater monitoring at World Cup venues to detect outbreaks five to seven days before symptoms appear clinically. Meanwhile, digital health access points are widening, including Dexcom's FDA clearance for an over-the-counter continuous glucose monitor for children and Medicare's coverage of weight loss drugs beginning next month. Healthcare systems are also grappling with infrastructure challenges, as coverage increasingly hinges on addressing rural transportation gaps and integrating autonomous systems and agentic AI tools across EHRs and clinical workflows.
